title: Tutorial
lead: Install the Skill, pick a mode, write prompts the agent can act on, and check the project files it should maintain. Sample prompts stay collapsed until you expand them.

walkthroughCta.title: Want the full project story?
walkthroughCta.body: Example walks Beginner and Designer lifecycles end to end: prompts, who does what, and sequence diagrams. It does not run the Skill.

start.title: What the Skill does
start.body: Board Game Design is an Agent Skill for evidence-driven tabletop design. You supply constraints, symptoms, and intent. The agent loads the smallest file set for the mode, writes templates into your project folder, and keeps Locked decisions, Claims, Evidence, and the experiment backlog in design-state.md.
start.habit: From session 2 onward, start with: read design-state first, then your request.

loop.title: Core loop
loop.note: Update design-state.md and repeat. Typical pipeline: concept, mechanism skeleton, cheapest valid prototype, playtest or balance, optional polish. Simulation output does not validate fun.

objects.title: Core objects
objects.lead: These show up in every mode. They are what persist across sessions.

items.name: State
items.body: design-state.md: Locked, Open, Rejected, Claims, Evidence, Target Player Model, experiment backlog.

items.name: Claim
items.body: Hypothesis with confidence, linked to EXP/HYP IDs.

items.name: Experiment
items.body: One variable, a baseline, a success metric, and a playtest-log link.

items.name: Prototype
items.body: Fidelity level (P0 to P5) and version, chosen for the hypothesis.

items.name: Artifact
items.body: Template outputs: concept-brief, mechanism-skeleton, simulation-run, rulebook bundle, decision.md, and related files.

checklist.title: Prompt checklist
items: Player count, duration, audience, target feel (MDA aesthetics)
New project or continuation (session 2+: say read design-state first)
For iteration: observed symptom and playtest evidence, not "make it better"
For tests: one variable and a measurable success metric
Optional: @file references to design-state, logs, or components

modes.title: Six modes
modes.lead: Use one mode per session. Each mode lists what to load, what to write, and two prompt styles: designer vocabulary, or player/beginner plain language.

designer.title: For professional game designers
designer.lead: You name mechanisms, symptoms, fidelity, and variables. Prompts assume you run playtests and read design-state between sessions.

beginner.title: For players and beginners
beginner.lead: You describe the game you want or what felt wrong at the table. Ask the agent to explain trade-offs in plain language, pick simple next steps, and write files to ./your-game/ so nothing dies in chat.

items.name: Create
items.writes: concept-brief.md, design-state.md (incl. Target Player Model), mechanism-skeleton.md
items.do: Compare 2 to 4 mechanism chassis before locking. Skip full rules on the first pass.
items.designerExample:
Design a 2-4 player, 45-minute medium-weight game about Mars colony logistics.
Target feel: scarcity tension, long-term planning, light direct conflict.
Audience: hobby gamers who know Wingspan but not heavy euros.
Compare worker placement vs action drafting vs open market. Recommend one with trade-offs.
Write concept-brief, design-state, and mechanism-skeleton to ./mars-habitat/ using templates/examples/micro-scavenger/ as format reference.
Do not write full rules yet.
items.beginnerExample:
I want a light board game for 3-4 friends, about 30-45 minutes, set in a cozy cat cafe we run together.
Vibe: funny, relaxed, a little competitive but no one should feel eliminated early.
Reference games we like: Ticket to Ride (easy to learn) and Unstable Unicorns (silly cards). I don't know terms like worker placement.
Compare 2-3 simple ways the game could work. Explain each in plain language before recommending one.
Write concept-brief, design-state, and mechanism-skeleton to ./cat-cafe/ using templates/examples/micro-scavenger/ as the file format.
No full rulebook yet.

items.name: Diagnose
items.when: Broken, boring, unfair, or forgettable play
items.load: routing/symptom-index.md, then cheatsheet.md, then diagnostics/* (BG* system or ED* experience)
items.writes: design-state.md; decision.md if you choose an intervention
items.do: Route the symptom, state one falsifiable hypothesis, pick the cheapest valid fidelity. Do not stack rule changes.
items.designerExample:
We've playtested 4 times (logs in ./orbital-mining/playtests/).
Leader is usually decided by round 3; trailing players say they can't catch up.
Read design-state first.
Diagnose snowball vs low agency vs endgame drag, propose one falsifiable hypothesis, and draft EXP-005.
Don't change three rules at once.
items.beginnerExample:
We played my draft 3 times with friends (notes in ./cat-cafe/playtests/).
By round 2 the same person is always ahead and the rest stop caring. Rules are in ./cat-cafe/mechanism-skeleton.md.
Read design-state first.
I'm not sure what's wrong. Tell me the most likely problem in plain language, propose ONE small change to try next, and write it up as an experiment draft.
Don't rewrite the whole game.

items.name: Experiment
items.when: Test one hypothesis with human play
items.do: Define baseline, one variable, and success metric. Update the experiment backlog in design-state.
items.designerExample:
Set up EXP-002: test hand limit 3 to 2 only. Everything else stays v0.6.
Hypothesis: smaller hand increases discard-pile fights without adding AP.
Success: in 4/5 playtests, both players contest discard at least twice; fun >= 3.5/5.
Write experiment.md and a blank playtest-log template for the next session.
items.beginnerExample:
Last playtest everyone said the starting hand is too random: some people open strong, others can't do anything.
Read design-state first.
Test ONLY one change: deal 5 cards instead of 7 at start. Keep all other rules the same.
Success: in the next 4 plays, at least 3 groups say everyone had a reasonable first turn.
Write experiment.md and a simple playtest-log I can fill in after game night.

items.name: Simulate
items.when: System metrics: win rate, game length, dominant strategy, population mix
items.do: Record seed, sample size, agent profiles, and confidence. Do not claim fun was validated.
items.designerExample:
Run 1000 mixed-population simulations of Micro Scavenger with seed 42.
Focus on length and seat win rates.
Write simulation-run.md and update design-state Evidence.
State explicitly that this is system evidence, not experience evidence.
items.beginnerExample:
My game always ends too fast and the first player wins too often, but I haven't playtested enough to be sure.
Read design-state first.
If a simulation can answer length and win-rate questions, run one and explain results in plain language. If paper playtests are better at this stage, say so and tell me what to track on the next 5 plays.
Do not change rules based on numbers alone.

items.name: Balance
items.when: Numbers, cards, economy, Effective Value Range
items.writes: balance-notes.md; balance-spreadsheet.md when numeric work is needed
items.do: One fix per pass. Link to an experiment or sim when testing one variable. Record confidence and dependencies.
items.designerExample:
Review CARD-014 through CARD-022 in ./deck-builder/components-sheet.md.
Build balance-spreadsheet rows using value-budget; flag any card where cost vs total estimated value differs by >40%.
State confidence, calibration source, use scope, and interaction/combo/timing dependency for each estimate.
items.beginnerExample:
I made 20 action cards in ./cat-cafe/components-sheet.md. Playtesters say a few cards are "broken" but I can't tell which.
Read design-state first.
Review the list, flag the 3 most likely outliers in plain language, and suggest adjusting ONE card first.
Write balance-notes.md. Skip heavy math unless it helps; explain your reasoning simply.

items.name: Prototype
items.when: Build at chosen fidelity, usually P4 paper PnP
items.writes: rulebook-draft.md, components-sheet.md, pnp-checklist.md (or a fidelity plan for lower rungs)
items.do: Run lint/checklist.md before P4 delivery. Export cards.csv when you need batch cards.
items.designerExample:
Turn ./v0.5/mechanism-skeleton.md into a paper PnP:
rulebook-draft, components-sheet, pnp-checklist.
2-4p, 30 min, index-card prototype, no art.
Export cards.csv per tools/export-pipeline.md if batch cards are needed.
Run lint/checklist before finishing.
items.beginnerExample:
I have a rough skeleton in ./cat-cafe/mechanism-skeleton.md. I want to print a playable version at home for game night.
2-4 players, about 30 minutes, index cards and paper tokens, no art needed.
Write rulebook-draft, components-sheet, and pnp-checklist I can print.
Use simple language a friend who hasn't read the design files can follow.

designerItems.label: Create: co-op with theme fit
designerItems.text:
Family co-op card game (2-4p, 20 min), Cthulhu investigation theme.
Core experience: dread and teamwork, not alpha-player quarterbacking.
Start with theme-and-experience (emotion curve), then suggest mechanisms that fit.
Output to ./deep-shallows/.

designerItems.label: Create: session 2+ (continue project)
designerItems.text:
Read design-state first in ./mars-habitat/.
We locked action drafting last session. Draft the core loop diagram and update mechanism-skeleton with the chosen chassis only.
Do not reopen worker placement unless new evidence.

designerItems.label: Diagnose: first-player advantage
designerItems.text:
After 3 sessions, seat 1 wins 5/7 games at 4 players. Hypothesis: first pick on the worker track is too strong.
Read design-state first. Run first-player-advantage diagnostic.
Smallest rule change to test next, with success criteria (seat 1 win rate < 35% over 10 plays).

designerItems.label: Experiment: rank backlog
designerItems.text:
Three hypotheses open in design-state (HYP-001 through HYP-003).
Read design-state first, rank with experiment-priority, update Experiment Backlog, draft EXP-004 for rank 1 only.

designerItems.label: Mixed request (symptom + PnP)
designerItems.text:
Playtests say the mid-game is dull AND I want a PnP by Friday.
Read design-state first. Diagnose mid-game drag first; do not jump to full PnP until we pick one hypothesis to test.

designerItems.label: Kill gate: after 3+ playtests
designerItems.text:
PT-001 through PT-004 done. Core loop is learnable but average fun was 2.8/5 twice in a row.
Run kill-criteria.md: Continue, Restructure, or Pause/Kill? Cite evidence.

designerItems.label: Mechanism lookup (no new files)
designerItems.text: Explain WPL-03 vs soft blocking (bumping) for a 2p game. Trade-offs only, no new project files.

beginnerItems.label: Create: idea from a story or hobby
beginnerItems.text:
I love hiking and want a game about planning a weekend trail with 2-5 friends, 45-60 min, cooperative but with light individual goals.
I don't know game design terms. Ask me up to 5 short questions if needed, then propose 2 simple structures and recommend one.
Save files to ./trail-weekend/. Plain-language summary at the top of concept-brief.

beginnerItems.label: Create: session 2+ (continue your game)
beginnerItems.text:
Read design-state first in ./cat-cafe/.
Last time we picked a card-drafting loop. This session: flesh out the skeleton with turn structure only. Still no full rulebook.
Explain changes in plain language.

beginnerItems.label: Diagnose: boring or confusing
beginnerItems.text:
We played twice. People said "it's fine" but nobody asked to play again, and two players didn't understand how to win until the end.
Read design-state first in ./my-game/.
Tell me the top 2 likely causes in plain language and ONE change to test next.

beginnerItems.label: Experiment: party game rule tweak
beginnerItems.text:
Our party game has a timer per turn. Test ONLY extending it from 30s to 45s.
Success: fewer skipped turns and average fun >= 3.5/5 over 3 playtests.
Write experiment.md and a one-page playtest sheet I can print.

beginnerItems.label: Prototype: first home print
beginnerItems.text:
I only have handwritten notes in ./my-game/notes.md.
Turn them into a minimal print-and-play: rules a new player can read in 5 minutes, card list, and what to cut from index cards.
No art, no fancy components.

beginnerItems.label: Kill gate: should I keep going?
beginnerItems.text:
We've playtested 5 times over a month. Friends are polite but enthusiasm is fading.
Read design-state and playtest notes in ./cat-cafe/.
In plain language: Continue, rethink the core idea, or stop? Cite what we actually observed, not guesses.

beginnerItems.label: I only know what I don't want
beginnerItems.text:
I want a family game for ages 10+. NOT heavy euro, NOT 3+ hours, NOT player elimination.
Theme open. Compare 2-3 light genres (party vs family coop vs set collection) in plain language.
Output to ./family-table/ with concept-brief and design-state only.

mixed.title: Mixed requests
mixed.body: When one prompt asks for design, PnP, and balance together, run Diagnose or Balance before Create or Prototype if symptoms exist. For system questions, run Simulate before large physical builds. Otherwise follow Create, then Prototype, then Balance. See cheatsheet.md for the priority tree.

invariants.title: Hard invariants
items: Read design-state first. Do not reopen Locked without new contradicting evidence.
Diagnose before changing rules: symptom and causal hypothesis first.
Minimal intervention: one variable per experiment, no stacked fixes.
Cheapest valid test first: lowest fidelity that can answer the hypothesis (prototype/fidelity-ladder.md).
System evidence is not experience evidence. Sims do not prove fun. Digital does not replace physical when physical_dependency is true.
Never auto-fix from a simulation anomaly. Follow Observation, Diagnostic, Hypothesis, Experiment.

milestones.title: Workflow milestones
milestones.lead: Milestones 0 to 5 from workflow.md. Regress when evidence requires it; this is not a one-way waterfall.

items.name: Concept
items.body: Pitch, MDA aesthetics, emotion curve, player count, playtime, audience. Output: concept-brief.md.

items.name: Core MVP
items.body: Paper loop, fun in one sentence. First human-playable build is usually P4.

items.name: Structure
items.body: Mechanism skeleton, spreadsheet data, candidate comparison.

items.name: Playtest
items.body: Experiments, playtest logs, kill gate. Allowed regressions: 3 to 1, 3 to 2.

items.name: Polish
items.body: Rulebook blind test, balance passes. Blind test failure returns to milestone 2.

genres.title: Genre profiles
genres.lead: In Create mode, load one genre-profile/ file and record it in design-state Project Status.

routing.title: Symptom routing
routing.body: Route vague symptoms through routing/symptom-index.md before diagnostics. System failures map to BG* codes (snowball, first-player advantage, dominant strategy, and others). Experience failures map to ED001 through ED008 (forgettable, generic, fantasy break, and others). Load the smallest matching diagnostic file, not every chapter.

items.action: Returns the SKILL.md overview and indexes.
Loads the chapter and the patterns.md entry.
Loads kill-criteria.md for Continue, Restructure, or Pause-or-Kill.

items.name: design-state.md
items.why: Single source of truth across sessions

items.name: concept-brief.md
items.why: Pitch, audience, Target Player Model, feel

items.name: mechanism-skeleton.md
items.why: Chassis, core loop, 2 to 4 candidate comparison

items.name: balance-notes.md + balance-spreadsheet.md
items.why: Effective Value Range, one fix per pass

fidelity.title: Fidelity ladder
fidelity.lead: The hypothesis selects the rung. P4 paper PnP is the usual first human-playable build.

items.name: Physical paper PnP, usual first playable

kill.title: Kill gate
kill.lead: After 3+ playtests, or if the core loop still fails after 2 weeks in Stage 1, run kill-criteria.md.

paths.name: Continue
paths.body: Core loop holds. Hypotheses are supported or fixable with single-variable experiments.

paths.name: Restructure
paths.body: Theme still works but the mechanism chassis does not. Return to Stage 1 or 2 and move failed mechanisms to Rejected.

paths.name: Pause or Kill
paths.body: Core premise fails. Archive the project and record learnings in design-state and iteration.md.

kill.note: Fun at or below 3/5 for two sessions, with feedback on the same mechanism, usually means chassis work, not more rules.

items.a: No. Design modes are Markdown only. runtime/ (bgd-sim) is optional for Monte Carlo on supported adapters such as Micro Scavenger.

items.q: Is this the Building Blocks book?
items.a: No. chapters/ contains synthesized trade-offs from Engelstein and Shalev, not a verbatim copy. Buy the book for the source text.

items.q: Where should I install the Skill?
items.a: Use a project-scoped path (.cursor/skills/, .claude/skills/, or .agents/skills/board-game-design/) when sharing a game repo. User-wide paths work for solo experiments.

items.q: Can sims prove the game is fun?
items.a: No. Sims answer system questions: win rate, length, dominance. Humans validate experience, tension, and clarity.
routing/context-budget.md defines required, optional, and forbidden file loads per mode so the agent does not bulk-load all 13 chapters.
Use templates/examples/micro-scavenger/ as the structure when starting a new game folder.
